articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Liverpool vs Manchester City
articles.standfirst: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Liverpool y Manchester City en Anfield correspondiente a la jornada 6 de la Premier League 2026-27
articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Liverpool y Manchester City en Anfield correspondiente a la jornada 6 de la Premier League 2026-27
articles.body: El Liverpool llega a esta sexta jornada de la Premier League después de imponerse por la mínima al Bournemouth en el regreso de Iraola al Vitality Stadium. Un solitario gol de Isak permitió al conjunto 'red' sumar tres puntos y mantener su condición de invicto... aunque su inicio de temporada está marcado por los empates: acumula tres por solamente dos victorias. Favorito para el partido entre Liverpool y Manchester City El Manchester City, por su parte, afronta este duelo después de una sufrida victoria frente al Sunderland antes del parón. Un resultado que permitió a los de Enzo Maresca marcharse como líderes de la Premier League y con un pleno de cinco victorias en las cinco primeras jornadas. El historial reciente entre ambos equipos presenta dos triunfos del Liverpool y tres del City en sus últimos cinco enfrentamientos. Las casas de apuestas sitúan el encuentro en un escenario muy igualado: 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 2.54 por la victoria del Liverpool, 3.68 por el empate y 2.57 por el triunfo del Manchester City. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una opción interesante en las apuestas deportivas... aunque los precedentes directos más recientes no apuntan en la misma dirección. El Liverpool solamente ha cumplido este pronóstico en dos de sus cinco primeros partidos de la temporada, mientras que el Manchester City lo ha hecho en tres de sus cinco encuentros. Además, únicamente en uno de los últimos cinco enfrentamientos entre ambos equipos marcaron los dos conjuntos. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.47 por el 'sí' y de 2.52 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) La línea de goles presenta una tendencia algo más favorable al over. El Liverpool solamente ha superado los 2.5 goles totales en dos de sus cinco primeros partidos, mientras que el Manchester City lo ha hecho en tres ocasiones. Además, esta barrera se ha alcanzado en tres de los cinco últimos duelos directos entre ambos equipos. Un registro que invita a esperar un partido con posibilidades de superar los 2.5 tantos. 1XBET paga a 1.53 que se marquen más de 2.5 goles y a 2.31 que se registren menos de 2.5 tantos. Goles en ambas mitades El mercado de goles en ambas mitades también presenta una tendencia ligeramente más favorable al Manchester City. Este escenario se ha producido en dos de los cinco primeros partidos del Liverpool, mientras que el conjunto de Pep Guardiola lo ha cumplido en tres de sus cinco encuentros. Además, también hubo goles en ambas partes en tres de los cinco últimos enfrentamientos directos entre Liverpool y Manchester City. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.52 por que haya goles en ambas mitades y de 2.36 por que no se produzca este escenario.

articles.title: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Live Updates, Results and Highlights
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Money in the Bank 2026.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Money in the Bank 2026.

Scroll down for updates covering the entire show, from pre-show to post-show, at the Smoothie King Center in New Orleans.

Evans going through the ambulance is definitely the most talked-about moment from MITB.

Penta and Tiffy both gave interviews with the post-show panel about winning.

Liv Morgan came away from this PLE as the new world champion, but the big stories will be Stratton and Penta winning the MITB briefcases.

Breakker stopped Evans from climbing and hit a gutbuster. He took down his straps and lined up for a Spear, but Evans caught him with a Red Dot kick instead. Evans climbed the ladder, but it was nowhere near the middle of the ring.

Bron laughed when he saw what he could do, and then he pushed the ladder over so Evans went crashing through the top of the ambulance for the most insane spot of the night. Evans hit that perfectly.

Penta and Breakker ended up climbing up the same side of the ladder that had another ladder set up like a bridge to the corner. Penta hit the Mexican Destroyer on the ladder and both men fell to the mat.

El Cero Miedo climbed up as the crowd went nuts for him. He took down the briefcase and became Mr. Money in the Bank.

Penta prevented Williams from climbing up the ladder. We got a shot backstage of Evans being put into an ambulance and driven away. Punk hit a back body drop on Owens onto a ladder, and then Penta took out Punk with his finisher.

Yachty distracted Breakker so Williams could bring him off the ladder and hit a slam. KO allowed Yachty to climb off the ladder before hitting him with a Stunner in the funniest moment of the match.

Penta ate a GTA from Punk, which left him open to climb up the ladder. Breakker started taking out each competitor with Spears one by one. Punk and Owens were fighting by the barricade, so Bron ran around the ring and Speared both men through the barricade.

An ambulance drove into the arena near the stage and up the aisle until it was up against the ring. Evans opened the door into Breakker's face to knock him down. Je'Von jumped onto him and started beating him with everything he had.

The Young OG hit a flurry of moves to Penta and Williams in the ring until both men were out. He set up one of the biggest ladders after clearing the others out of the ring.

Breakker ended up suplexing Penta while Penta was already holding Punk, making it a two-for-one. A ladder was finally set up for the first time. Owens stopped Evans from climbing and threw him out of the ring, and then he had to stop Punk from reaching the case.

Trick tried to quickly climb the ladder, but Breakker was there to stop him. Bron ran across the barricade and announce table before leaping onto Williams. He stood on the table to gloat, and then Owens tripped him off the table.

Punk, Owens, Penta and Williams all ended up in the timekeeper's area, so Evans took a lap around the ring to dive onto all of them, but he was cut in half by a Spear from Breakker.

Punk went back into the ring to climb the ladder, but Bron was right there to stop him. Medics arrived with a stretcher for Evans. He was wheeled away as Owens and Punk fought in the ring.

Owens tried to hurt Punk any way he could with the ladders, including a spinebuster onto one.

The men's Money in the Bank match included CM Punk, Kevin Owens, Trick Williams, Je'Von Evans, Penta and Bron Breakker. Punk was the first to make his entrance. Lil Yachty was there with Williams. Penta was the final man to enter the ring.

Breakker took out Penta during his signature pose to kick-start the action. It came down to Punk and Owens, who started brawling until Breakker took them both down.

Punk went after Trick and mocked his dance, but Williams took him down and mocked him right back. Yachty helped him put a huge ladder on the apron before Punk hit Trick with a suicide dive.

Evans hit a huge leap over a ladder Owens was holding to take Punk down. Everyone was fighting at ringside and nobody seemed to be able to get a ladder all the way in until Penta brought one in.

Breakker put a ladder in the corner and whipped Punk into it while screaming in his face. Penta appeared to be limping when he got back into the ring. KO blocked a bulldog and dropped Punk onto a ladder.

Vaquer vs. Morgan vs. Lynch (World Title) Part 3

Vaquer hit both women with meteroras against the steel steps at ringside. She hit Morgan with a twisting moonsault, but Lynch pulled the ref out of the ring to stop the count.

A table had been set up at ringside earlier, and Vaquer sent Lynch crashing onto it with a superkick, but it didn't break.

Morgan caught Vaquer with Oblivion out of nowhere and pinned her to regain the world title.

Vaquer vs. Morgan vs. Lynch (World Title) Part 2

Vaquer hit Morgan with the Devil's Kiss, and then she hit a brutal dragon screw over the ring rope for a two-count. Lynch tried to come in and take over, but the champ took her down for a near-fall, too.

Vaquer dropped Lynch onto Morgan and then hit a crossbody for a two-count. Morgan sold a backbreaker well, but still kicked out. Lynch hit the Bexploder on Vaquer, followed by a German suplex to Morgan.

She spiked both women with a double DDT, but neither would stay down for the three-count. There was an awkward moment with Lynch and Vaquer in the corner when it seemed like they couldn't decide what to do next.

La Primera locked Morgan in a half crab, but The Man put Liv in the DisArmHer, too, but neither got the win. All three women came close to winning a few times, but there was always someone else there to break it up.

Stephanie Vaquer vs. Liv Morgan vs. Becky Lynch (Women's World Championship) Part 1

Up next is the women's world title bout with Stephanie Vaquer defending against Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch. The Man was out first, followed by Liv. The champ was out last, and it felt like the crowd gave Lynch the biggest reaction, but La Primera had her fans, too.

Lynch and Vaquer took out Morgan with a double clothesline so they could square off together. They traded some simple takedowns and counters, but Morgan eventually came back in and attacked both of them.

When Liv tried her finisher on Becky, she was yanked out of the ring by Stephanie and sent into the barricade. Morgan hit a sunset flip powerbomb from the apron to the floor that took out The Man.

Reed slammed Femi with a Death Valley Driver, but when he went for a moonsault, Femi moved. He knocked Theory off the apron when he tried to get involved, and then he started building up a head of steam.

He powered Reed up and hit the Fall Grom Grace for the win.

Reed hit a few sentons when he got Femi back in the ring, but it wasn't enough to finish the match. Oba popped up and almost powered Reed up for a suplex, but his back was too hurt to get him up.

For the next couple of minutes, it felt like Reed had an answer for everything Femi tried. Oba rolled out of the way to avoid a Tsunami, and then he nailed Reed with a running uppercut. Big Bronson hit him with a DDT and then went back up to hit the Tsunami, but he missed when Femi moved again.

Femi caught Reed when he tried a corner splash, and he planted him with a spinebuster for a quick two-count. Austin Theory showed up and distracted Femi. The ref caught Logan Paul trying to come in with a chair and ejected The Vision from ringside.

Maxxine Dupri slid Reed a set of brass knuckles, which he used to rock Oba with two big right hands. He climbed up and hit the Tsunami, but Femi managed to kick out at two.

Two huge powerhouses collided in the third match when Oba Femi took on Bronson Reed. Surprisingly, nobody else from The Vision accompanied Reed to the ring. Paul Heyman was seen watching from backstage.

The bell rang and the behemoths stared each other down before literally colliding and beginning to throw punches. Reed got Femi in the corner for a knee to the body, but he failed to knock him down with a clothesline.

Bronson went to the well one too many times and ended up being knocked on his back. Femi countered a suplex and launched Reed across the ring in a way nobody has ever thrown him before.

They traded strikes on the apron until Reed planted The Ruler with a side suplex. He got back in the ring and hit Femi with a suicide dive that leveled him.

The ladder Vice and Jayne were on ended up falling out of the ring, and they tumbled out with it. It was a nasty looking spot that they did not seem prepared for.

Perez almost got to the top of the ladder, but Ruca caught up to her and hit the Sol Snatcher off the ladder. She tried to hurry up the ladder, but Legend grabbed her and hit a powerbomb onto the ladder.

Legend and Stratton each climbed a different side of the ladder and fought. Tiffy knocked Lash down and took down the briefcase to become a two-time MITB winner.

Vice took out a few competitors before Perez sent a ladder into her face by stomping on one end while it was hanging over the ropes. Roxy positioned Legend and Ruca on the ladder after some awkward moments, and she hit them both with a moonsault.

Stratton hit an Alabama slam on Perez before attempting to climb the ladder. Ruca springboarded onto the other side of the ladder so they could fight, but Jayne tipped the ladder over. Tiffy fell to her feet, but Ruca hung from the briefcase for a moment before falling onto everyone.

Legend chokeslammed Stratton and Perez onto a ladder and then began to climb. Ruca brought her back down and she ended up on the bridge ladder, which Ruca put her through with a huge splash from the top rope.

Back in the ring, Jayne drilled Vice with a knee so she could cimb, but Vice got back up and followed her.

The field for this year's match included Tiffany Stratton, Jacy Jayne, Lash Legend, Roxanne Perez, Lola Vice and Sol Ruca. Every competitor got a full entrance, and the first match was pretty long, so the second bout of the night didn't begin until an hour into the show.

When the bell rang, Legend was targeted by all five of her opponents, but it only took a few seconds before others started fighting each other too. Jayne set a ladder up between the ring and announce table like a bridge.

Stratton hit a swanton from the top of a ladder onto everyone else on the floor, and the landing looked especially brutal for her. The upper half of her body hit before her legs. Officials checked on her and all of the action came to a halt.

Jayne set up a ladder in the ring, but Tiffy was the first one to go after her. Perez found a very short ladder and started using it as a weapon, but one kick from Legend sent it crashing into her face.

Stratton and Ruca exchanged a series of counters that ended with Sol dropping Tiffy onto a ladder.

Some shots of Superstars preparing for the MITB matches were shown, as well as the obligatory celebrity shots in the crowd. The women's Money in the Bank match is up next. Tiffany Stratton was the first to make her entrance.

The Tribal Chief celebrated his win, but he spotted The 946 in the crowd. Royce Keys pointed at his watch to indicate that Roman's time is coming up, but that is when The Usos and Solo Sikoa showed up behind them.

The six men squared off, then began brawling through the stands. Solo and Keys fought while the Usos and OTM paired up and brawled. They battled all the way out of the arena onto the sidewalk.

Jaida Parker pulled up in a vehicle and The 946 took off with her.

Knight sent Reigns into the steel steps before bringing him to the announce table. Roman prevented a suplex and they started trading punches. Both men were almost counted out, but they made it back in before 10.

The OTC drilled Knight with a Superman Punch, but when he went for a Spear, Knight grabbed him with a BFT. Reigns barely kicked out at two, which Michael Cole said it might be the first time someone has kicked out of the move.

Roman ended up hitting a Spear out of nowhere, but it was only good enough for a near-fall. An irate champion began beating on Knight and screaming at him. He ran the ropes for another Spear, but Knight hit him with one instead.

The fight went outside the ring again, and Reigns ended up crashing through the barricade when he missed a Spear. Knight almost dropped him, but he was able to put him through the announce table with a powerbomb.

LA hit an elbow drop from the top rope, but he still couldn't keep the champ down for the pin. Reigns recovered and hit a Superman Punch, followed by a second. He finally hit a proper Spear to put Knight away for the win.

Knight sent Reigns into the ring post before he started taking apart the announce table. Roman recovered and brought him back into the ring before the table could come into play.

The Megastar made a comeback and scored a near-fall. The OTC nailed a Superman Punch, but he couldn't get the pin. He began to hype up the crowd as he set up in the corner for his trademark Spear.

Knight jumped over him and Reigns went right into the ring post. LA sat him on the top turnbuckle and climbed up for a superplex. Reigns tried to fight him off, but Knight hit it on the second attempt.

The challenger was unable to get the pin with a burning hammer. Roman came back at him with a uranage, but it only got a two-count.

Roman Reigns vs. LA Knight (World Heavyweight Championship) Part 1

We're kicking things off with the men's world title bout between Roman Reigns and LA Knight. The Megastar was out first, and he got a nice reaction from the NOLA crowd, but the reaction for The OTC was louder.

As usual, Roman took his sweet time getting to the ring. Byron Saxton was doing the ring announcing for the introduction.

When they finally locked up, Reigns put Knight in a headlock, and then he scored the first takedown with a shoulder tackle. Knight popped up and caught him off guard before taking him out, which sent Roman out of the ring to regroup.

He took most of the 10-count to get back in. Knight put him in a headlock, but Reigns avoided the shoulder tackle and jumped over him so he could hit a hip toss.

Reigns stayed aggressive and started to build some momentum. He lined up in the corner for the Superman Punch, but Knight ducked and hit a series of jabs.

LA telegraphed a back body drop and took a kick to the face, but then he sent Reigns out of the ring so they could continue the fight at ringside.

Money in the Bank opened with various shots of Superstars arriving at the arena throughout the day.

Roman Reigns has demanded to open Money in the Bank, which is likely so he can avoid the hassle of dealing with someone trying to cash in during or after his match. Alix Paige sang the Star-Spangled Banner before the show.

The pre-show is underway and the main card begins in less than 15 minutes.

articles.title: Stupaczuk y Sanz ahondan en la herida de Chingalán y repiten final
articles.standfirst: La pareja dos vuelve a no llegar a una final en la que sí estarán los números uno, Coello y Tapia, que amplián aún más la distancia en la Race.
articles.summary: La pareja dos vuelve a no llegar a una final en la que sí estarán los números uno, Coello y Tapia, que amplián aún más la distancia en la Race.
articles.body: Reabrieron la herida de Chingalán en Rotterdam y en Düsseldorf han ahondado en ella. Franco Stupaczuk y Jon Sanz han vuelto a eliminar a Ale Galán y Fede Chingotto, esta vez en semifinales. Una victoria sufrida, muy sufrida, y que han vendido cara la pareja dos que aún tocada y casi hundida, no negocia el sacrificio y si se han dejado en Alemania su penúltima bala de acertar al número uno del año es por mérito rival. Porque Sanz y Stupa funcionan. Hasta ahora podía haber alguna duda, cierto recelo sobre el tiempo o el factor sorpresa, pero lo cierto es que se entienden, carburan y logran lo más importante de todo, hacer equipo. Lo harían desde el arranque del partido y durante un primer set ajustado, de intercambios, donde solo el tie-break daría la merecida ventaja a los de Cristian Arias por la mínima en una muerte súbita que gestionarían mejor (7-6). Y ahí, parecería acabado el partido. Con Stupa de nuevo en esa versión prime, de fallo nulo, mucha versatilidad e ida y vuelta, y Sanz suelto en la ofensiva y haciendo daño a Chingotto, tomarían ventaja en el segundo set para encarar la definición del partido. Se tendrían que agarrar al vértido pues tras tres opciones de partido, primero, que se irían al limbo, sentirían la presión rival al lograr un contrabreak que parecía una quimera para, finalmente, volver a dar el golpe de gracia cuando todo hacía pensar en la igualada. Por 7-6 y 6-4 lograrían la segunda clasificación a una final consecutiva volviendo a dejar por el camino a la pareja dos que tendrá que pensar ya en Milán, su última opción de mantenerse en la pelea, mientras ellos buscan su primer campeonato. Título que buscarán evitar los dominadores del circuito, los números uno, que no fallan. Con la de Alemania van ya 16 finales en 18 torneos disputados, unos números que quieren acrecentar con su título número 11 de la temporada este domingo. Otra vez lo harían eliminando a Leo Augsburger y Juan Lebrón, pareja tres, que no acabaron de encontrar su mejor versión en semifinales y lo pagarían caro ante unos Golden Boys que ya han puesto la directa en la temporada y no van a dejar que nadie se suba al tren. El 6-2 y 6-3 en apenas una hora de partido definiría a la perfección lo que sería una exhibición de los de Martín Canali con un Tapia de nuevo enchufado a la fuente de inspiración y un Coello que, sin tanto brilla, clava esto del pádel.

images.caption: Jon y Stupa celebran el triunfo. PREMIER PADEL

articles.title: Oba Femi Beats Bronson Reed, Predicting The Ruler's Next Top Matches After WWE Money in the Bank
articles.summary: Oba Femi beat Bronson Reed in a grudge match at WWE Money in the Bank on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Oba Femi beat Bronson Reed in a grudge match at WWE Money in the Bank on Saturday night.

This was a tough match between two powerful men.

Reed went airborne early to take down Femi.

Reed later landed a Tsunami, but Femi somehow kicked out.

A ferocious Femi was too tough in the end. He chokeslammed an interfering Austin Theory before tossing Reed and hitting him with the Fall From Grace for the win.

Femi vs. Reed had been in the works for over a month, dating back to Reed's surprise return from injury during Femi's match against Bron Breakker at Sunday Night's Main Event on Sept. 6.

Reed came to the aid of his Vision stablemate, attacking Femi with a steel chair and causing a disqualification.

Femi and Reed continued to clash in the weeks that followed Sunday Night's Main Event, but Bronson often had backup in the form of The Vision.

On the Raw after SNME, the entire group brutally attacked Femi, including Reed, who laid him out with multiple Tsunami splashes.

At the end of the segment, Reed even placed his foot atop the prone Femi, just as Oba had done to Brock Lesnar during his heated rivalry with The Beast Incarnate.

However, Femi swatted Reed's foot away as he lay on the mat.

That situation added to the intrigue surrounding the match and another layer to their storyline rivalry.

Either way, Saturday's win was a huge one for The Ruler, as he remains on track for an eventual world title opportunity.

In terms of what might be next for Femi, another clash with Breakker seems plausible since there was not a decisive finish to their first match.

Another thing to keep an eye on is Femi possibly participating in a WarGames match at Survivor Series in November. With two major feuds dominating Raw, perhaps Femi joining forces with The Bloodline to face The Vision and The 946 could be in the cards.

articles.title: Penta Wins 2026 WWE Money in the Bank Men's Ladder Match in New Orleans
articles.summary: Penta won the 2026 men's Money in the Bank ladder match at the Money in the Bank premium live event on Saturday.
articles.body:
Penta won the 2026 men's Money in the Bank ladder match at the Money in the Bank premium live event on Saturday.

Penta outlasted a stacked field in New Orleans, beating out Bron Breakker, Je'Von Evans, Kevin Owens, CM Punk and Trick Williams to secure the Money in the Bank briefcase.

By virtue of his victory, the luchador earned the right to challenge for the WWE Championship or World Heavyweight Championship at any time or place of his choosing within the next year.

Penta won after hitting Breakker with a Mexican Destroyer off one ladder and then onto a second ladder below.

This match also featured a wild spot in which Breakker pushed Evans, who was atop a ladder, out of the ring and through the roof of an ambulance parked next to the squared circle.

Breakker had left Evans needing medical help after hitting him with a devastating spear.

Evans was taken away from New Orleans' Smoothie King Center in an ambulance, but The Young OG didn't find his way to the hospital.

Instead, he drove the vehicle back to the ring with his sights set on Breakker.

Other moments included Kevin Owens giving Lil Yachty, who was trying to help Williams, a Stunner.

Owens and CM Punk spent much of their time in this match fighting each other, and their animosity was abundantly clear from the very beginning.

Breakker's brutality was also present, and he inflicted a heap of pain on everyone involved.

No one was exempt from his spears in the latter portion of the match.

In the end, though, Penta was victorious.

A series of Triple Threat qualifying matches were held in the weeks leading up to Money in the Bank to determine the participants in Saturday's bout.

Breakker got the better of Rey Mysterio and Ethan Page, Evans beat Big Cass and Austin Theory, Williams outlasted Randy Orton and Rey Fenix, Penta defeated Dominik Mysterio and Dragon Lee, Punk took down Gunther and Finn Balor, and Owens bested Cody Rhodes and Johnny Gargano.

This year's men's Money in the Bank ladder match featured multiple Superstars who were looking to take the next step and put themselves in the conversation as a potential future world champ.

While winning Money in the Bank doesn't guarantee a world title win, there are few better ways for a wrestler to position themselves than securing the Money in the Bank contract.

Becoming Mr. Money in the Bank means getting to dictate the terms of a title match at any time, often putting the champion in a highly precarious position.

Penta is fresh off a World Heavyweight Championship match against Roman Reigns on Raw in Mexico City, and although he didn't come out on top, he pushed The Tribal Chief to the limit.

After proving he belonged in the world title and main event mix, Penta has a chance to cement himself in those conversations if he can cash in his Money in the Bank contract successfully.

articles.title: Marner scores on OT power play to lift the Golden Knights past the Kings, 2-1
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Mitch Marner scored a power-play goal from the high slot at 2:41 of overtime to give Vegas a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Satur...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — Mitch Marner scored a power-play goal from the high slot at 2:41 of overtime to give Vegas a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday on a night in which the Golden Knights paid tribute to their past.

Trevor Connelly scored the other goal for the Golden Knights, and he, Marner and Mark Stone each produced two points, with Stone getting both of his on assists. Carter Hart made 26 saves.

Artemi Panarin scored for the Kings, with Darcy Kuemper stopping 30 shots.

Vegas (5-1) is off to a quick start this season, and Los Angeles (0-2-2) is still searching for its first victory.

Each club swapped power-play goals in the second period, with the 20-year-old rookie Connelly punching in the puck after Stone's pinpoint cross-ice and Panarin answering with a shot from the high slot.

In overtime, the Golden Knights quickly took advantage of a tripping penalty on Kings center Scott Laughton. Marner skated from near the blue line toward the slot, depositing the puck just seven seconds into the penalty.

The Golden Knights, now in their 10th season, paid tribute throughout the game to their inaugural team known as the "Misfits." Gerard Gallant, who coached that team that made it to the Stanley Cup Final, was in attendance along with several players. Fan favorite Ryan Reaves, who retired last month after 16 NHL seasons, cranked the pregame siren.

Referee Furman South briefly went down to the ice early in the third period when Vegas center Nic Dowd collided with him. South got up holding his midsection, but remained in the game.

Golden Knights: At Minnesota on Monday night.

articles.title: Darcy Kuemper's Heroics Wasted In Kings Overtime Loss
articles.summary: There is still a lot of the season left after a winless first week, but Saturday night's loss to the Vegas Golden Knights was very frustrating to watch.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper, back on the crease, delivered one of his best games in a long time, posting his best season performance with several big saves against the Vegas Golden Knights and easing pressure on the Kings' defense.

The 36-year-old posted 30 saves on 32 shots on Saturday night, anchoring LA's defense on the road against a Western Conference opponent. But it still wasn't enough to give the Kings their first road win of the season in a tough environment.

The Kings have now started the season off 0-2-2 for the first time in franchise history. Somehow, though, even though they played arguably their best against a quality team, this loss feels much harder to swallow given how close the match came down.

By all means, this was a very winnable game for the visiting team; despite never leading, the Kings were in position to take the lead, especially with Kuemper's crease play giving the offense plenty of chances to take over.

The game was tied 1-1 after 40 minutes, thanks to Kuemper's strong goaltending, and Artemi Panarin tied the score with a power-play goal in the second period.

The final period mirrored the opening, with both teams struggling to score and their defenses tightening to stretch the game as long as possible. LA was doing a solid job on the rush, especially on the 3-on-2 break-up, with Drew Doughty stopping a dangerous situation.

Neither team could control the game or take the lead in the third period to break the tie. For the second time this season, the Kings were headed to extra periods in T-Mobile Arena.

In overtime, back-to-back plays by Adrian Kempe and Quinton Byfeild looked like they would lead to a game-winning goal and head home, but a big save by Knights goaltender Carter Hart kept the home team alive.

All those chances, the door was left open for the home team to convert, and they did. Off the faceoff, Mitch Marner spotted the traffic and nailed a shot down the middle, converting on the Knights' power play and finishing 2/3.

After the game, winner Kuemper, who left it all on the ice, walked off, disappointed, shrugging in disbelief after his best game of the season.

A disappointing season last year and an ugly start to this one, despite playing better tonight, have turned up the volume about ownership and whether this team should move towards rebuilding rather than staying in the middle for the last 10 years already.

Despite the defense playing its best this season, holding Vegas to a season-low two goals, the Kings' offense let them down, especially in the final period, after the defense made quality saves and stops; they failed to capitalize.

While the Kings played another close one and looked like they wanted it more, the box score didn't show it. They once again struggled on the power play, finishing 1-for-3 and scoring just one goal in their second straight game.

The positive takeaway from this game was that Kuemper looked excellent on the road against the Knights. If he continues this play, all LA needs to do is work on their offense, and the team will be fine.

articles.title: No. 2 Georgia defeats No. 6 Alabama, first win in Tuscaloosa since 2007
articles.summary: No. 2 Georgia held on to defeat No. 6 Alabama on Saturday night.
articles.body:
No. 2 Georgia held on to defeat No. 6 Alabama, 20-17, on Saturday night.

Georgia's defense forced Alabama to punt and Gunner Stockton led the offense in running out the clock in the final minutes. Peyton Woodring scored the game-winning field goal with five minutes to go.

It's the first time since 2007 that the Georgia defeated Alabama in the regular season in Tuscaloosa.

With No. 1 Texas losing to Oklahoma, the Dawgs are certain to become the new No. 1 team when the Associated Press poll is released Sunday afternoon.

articles.title: Maple Leafs Goaltender Sergei Bobrovksky Earns First Win With His New Team
articles.summary: After a rough start to his tenure with the Toronto Maple Leafs, Sergei Bobrovsky finally earned his first win with his new team. The post Maple Leafs Goalten...
articles.body:
After a rough start to his tenure with the Toronto Maple Leafs, Sergei Bobrovsky finally earned his first win. It was definitely a sigh a relief for Bobrovsky and Maple Leafs supporters.

Bobrovsky was excellent in net, as he kept Toronto in the game with several big stops. The two-time Stanley Cup winner entered tonight's matchup against the Colorado winless in three starts.

Bobrovsky held a 0-2-1 record, having lost his most recent start against the Vegas Golden Knights in a shootout.

Maple Leafs Goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky Earns First Win With His New Team

Sergei Bobrovsky was the difference-maker in the Maple Leafs' 6-3 victory over the Avalanche.

Bobrovsky made 30 saves on 33 shots faced and finished the game with an impressive .909 save percentage. He was heavily relied on, as the Avalanche's offense were firing on all cylinders.

While the Leafs picked up an early lead, the Avalanche answered with two goals to take the lead going into the first intermission.

Toronto responded in the second period, scoring three goals to go up 4-3 going into the third period. The Leafs stayed composed and closed out the victory by adding a pair of goals.

Colorado entered tonight's game with the best goal differential in the NHL so far, with a +12. Given some of the Avalanche's dominant wins so far this season, Bobrovsky holding the team to only three goals made his victory even more impressive.

articles.title: Former Los Angeles Lakers Center Primed for Big Minutes to Start 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: After three seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers, Jaxson Hayes left this summer and joined the Utah Jazz.ESPN’s Tim MacMahon was the first to report Hayes’ de...
articles.body:
After three seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers, Jaxson Hayes left this summer and joined the Utah Jazz.

ESPN's Tim MacMahon was the first to report Hayes' decision to sign a two-year contract with the Jazz.

"Source: The Jazz are signing former Lakers center Jaxson Hayes to a two-year, $12 million deal. The second season is a team option," MacMahon tweeted.

In 192 games with the Lakers, Hayes averaged 6.2 points and 3.9 rebounds per game on 73.5 percent shooting.

Hayes Could Have Big Role Early This Season

The Utah Jazz signed Jaxson Hayes to be the team's backup center behind Jusuf Nurkic .

However, Nurkic suffered an injury in the Jazz's first preseason game against the Denver Nuggets last week. He was ruled out for at least four weeks, which meant he could miss around eight games to start the season.

According to Shreyas Laddha of the Salt Lake City Tribune , Hayes could provide a pivotal role for the Jazz as a starting center.

"Hayes' value on offense mostly comes as a lob threat, and he showed good chemistry with the Jazz guards in the preseason pick-and-roll," Laddha wrote. "Expect to see plenty of that in the coming weeks. Hayes ranked in the 98th percentile in two-point percentage last year."

Hayes played well alongside Luka Doncic during his time with the Los Angeles Lakers as a lob threat. He would now be working with Keyonte George in the starting lineup and Isaiah Collier off the bench.

Laddha added that once Nurkic returns from injury, Hayes has already developed chemistry with Collier during training camp. Collier and Hayes could be one of the most lethal pick-and-roll duos off the bench in the NBA .

It's worth pointing out that Kyle Filipowski underwent back surgery this past offseason. He was cleared for training camp, but he will likely be limited as a way to ease him back into full-contact basketball.

Hayes on Stepping Up Amid Nurkic's Absence

Speaking to The Salt Lake City Tribune , Hayes addressed his new role in the absence of Nurkic for the next month or so. He used his experience with the Los Angeles Lakers to explain his mentality heading into his first season in Utah.

"It's the next-man-up mentality," Hayes said. "I dealt with some of these issues in LA, so just staying prepared and being a professional. Everybody has got to be ready, so just going to come do my job."

The Jazz have two more preseason games remaining against the San Antonio Spurs and Phoenix Suns . They open the regular season on October 21 against the Memphis Grizzlies .

articles.title: Why Lane Kiffin isn’t too surprised by LSU’s loss to Kentucky – ‘you don’t execute, you don’t execute’
articles.summary: LSU coach Lane Kiffin was not surprised by his team’s mistakes in its 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky on Saturday. The No. 10 Tigers had chances to close out...
articles.body:
LSU coach Lane Kiffin was not surprised by his team's mistakes in its 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky on Saturday. The No. 10 Tigers had chances to close out the game but failed to make key plays. The Wildcats pulled off an upset at Kroger Field.

Kiffin pointed to missed tackles and poor execution as major reasons LSU could not hold on to its lead. Kentucky scored a late field goal to force overtime before winning with a two-point conversion.

"I mean, not really. If you don't execute the punt return, got a player there tackling them, and he doesn't tackle them, and it goes outside in the long run," Kiffin said. "So if you don't do fundamentally sound stuff, you get exposed versus good teams."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

LSU led 27-24 with 97 seconds left in regulation, but Kentucky drove 63 yards in 1 minute, 25 seconds to set up the game-tying field goal. The Wildcats then matched LSU's touchdown in overtime and scored on quarterback Kenny Minchey's two-point run to secure the 35-34 victory.

LSU dropped to 4-2 overall and 1-2 in SEC play after the defeat. However, both defeats came on the road , extending the Tigers' conference road losing streak to eight games. Their last SEC road win came against Arkansas on October 19, 2024.

LSU's offense produced 410 total yards, including 316 passing yards, but its running game struggled. The Tigers managed just 94 yards on 36 rushing attempts. Quarterback Sam Leavitt completed 25 of 34 passes for 275 yards and two touchdowns, but he also committed a turnover.

Penalties added to LSU's problems. The Tigers were flagged seven times for 50 yards, while Kentucky had two penalties for 20 yards.

articles.title: In Photos: Nabil Anane Unveils A Fresh Look And Full Arsenal At ONE SAMURAI 4 Open Workout
articles.summary: The 6-foot-4 skyscraper displayed some of the weapons he has ready for Yuki Yoza on October 17!
articles.body:
A new haircut signals a fresh start for former ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion Nabil Anane .

Coming off back-to-back losses for the first time in his ONE Championship career, the Algerian-Thai skyscraper returns to kickboxing for a bantamweight showdown with Japanese superstar Yuki Yoza at ONE SAMURAI 4 , live from Tokyo's Ariake Arena on Saturday, October 17.

Japanese fans can attend the event in person or watch live via U-NEXT. Meanwhile, international fans can watch the blockbuster spectacle exclusively on live.onefc.com .

This past Wednesday, October 7, Anane welcomed the media to his home base, Venum Training Camp in Pattaya, Thailand, for a high-tempo open workout. He also showed off his shorter hairstyle, the result of a pre-fight vow to shave his head if he lost to Suakim Pongsuphan PK at The Inner Circle 25 in August.

The 22-year-old utilized every inch of his towering 6-foot-4 frame during the pad sessions, unleashing his pterodactyl-like length with rangy hooks, spear-like jabs, laser straight punches, and deceptive question mark kicks that cracked throughout the gym. Anane also flashed his work inside the pocket, chaining uppercuts and short hooks that should prove useful against the forward-pressing Yoza.

Following the intense workout, the Algerian-Thai striker strapped the gloves back on, putting the ONE x Venum global apparel and glove partnership front and center for the cameras.

With ONE SAMURAI 4 less than a week away, he put on his game face and stared down the camera lens with a quiet intensity. Then, he fielded questions from reporters, showing a maturity and poise that belied his age.

The Algerian-Thai phenom became the youngest-ever WBC Muay Thai World Champion at 17 and then made his mark in the promotion with career-defining wins over Nico Carrillo and former two-sport king Superlek to eventually become the undisputed ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion. His latest victory came in kickboxing, where he outpointed Hiromi Wajima in a featherweight contest at ONE 173 .

A win over Yoza – a recent World Title challenger – could put Anane in contention for 26 pounds of gold in a second sport. That belt will be on the line in the main event, as ONE Bantamweight Kickboxing World Champion Jonathan "The General" Haggerty defends it against Hiroki Akimoto .

Before he makes the trek back to Tokyo, check out the photos from his open workout in Pattaya.

articles.title: How Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning faltered as 'Texas beat Texas'
articles.summary: Arch Manning's turnovers and Steve Sarkisian's late decisions doomed No. 1 Texas in a stunning 27-24 Red River loss to Oklahoma.
articles.body:
DALLAS - Steve Sarkisian didn't trust his quarterback, and he didn't trust his play caller.

Then, given a second chance in the closing minutes at the Cotton Bowl, both went out and proved his doubts right.

By this point, after Saturday's 27-24 Red River reckoning in which the top-ranked Texas Longhorns confirmed one narrative after another while losing to Oklahoma, it's probably time to acknowledge that we know exactly who they are.

The quarterback, Arch Manning, can make every spectacular throw suggested by his bloodline, and can dice up any defense in the country under pressure. But for every couple of "Holy Moly!" completions, he's going to produce an inexplicable "Holy Moly!" misfire.

The play caller, who happens to be Sarkisian himself, understands offense like few coaches in the world do. But at the most inopportune moments - at the goal line in the national semifinals, for instance - he's prone to freeze up, too.

That shouldn't be surprising anymore, either.

So a month after the college football world saw Manning and Sarkisian at their best in an improbable comeback against Ohio State, we probably should have seen Saturday's equally improbable collapse coming.

And when the Longhorns' best player was asked to explain why one of the most talented teams in the sport lost to their deservedly unranked, thoroughly unspectacular archrivals?

"I think Texas beat Texas," defensive end Colin Simmons said.

Texas beat Texas in ways that have become all too familiar during the Sarkisian era, which has been marked by a series of unquestionable steps forward interspersed with mystifying stumbles.

Penalties proved costly. Special teams were a mess. And a coach who takes pride in boldness picked the weirdest possible occasion to get conservative.

This time, it came at the two-minute warning, with the score tied and the Longhorns facing fourth-and-2 at the Oklahoma 35. For all intents and purposes, a first down there wins the game. To get it, all Texas needed was two yards from an offense featuring an Hall of Fame-pedigree passer, and (allegedly) $4 million worth of wide receivers, and two high-profile transfer running backs, and a left tackle projected to go in the first round of the NFL draft.

But Sarkisian didn't try to gain those two yards. He chose instead to attempt a 53-yard field goal, which - best-case scenario - would have left 1:55 on the scoreboard for the Sooners to win the game against a tiring Texas defense.

Later, Sarkisian said his decision came down to one question:

"Did I think we had a really good play call that could get us the first down?" he said.

How does the No. 1 team in the country, with all of those gifted options, not have that kind of play call? Why wouldn't Sarkisian trust himself to pick one? And why wouldn't he trust in Manning to carry it out?

Well, it wasn't long before we found out. After the Longhorns' field-goal attempt sailed wide right, the Texas defense held. But given the ball again with 54 seconds left, Manning couldn't take advantage.

Just like earlier in the quarter, when he made a bad decision and a worse throw on an airmailed interception that was returned 42 yards for an Oklahoma touchdown, Manning panicked and got picked off again.

Under heavy pressure from his right side, he looked left at first, then apparently didn't get a good look at cornerback Courtland Guillory's positioning when he fired the ball back to his right.

Guillory made the diving interception, and then Oklahoma got two beautiful sideline grabs to set up the 47-yard game-winning kick from Tate Sandell, the transfer from UTSA.

The celebration that ensued probably will turn out to be the highlight of the season for the Sooners, who weren't championship contenders when they arrived at the State Fair and almost certainly weren't contenders when they left, either.

With 12 playoff spots up for grabs, the Longhorns remain firmly in that group. Their victory over the Buckeyes will go a long way toward giving them the benefit of the doubt, even if they absorb another loss or two.

The question is, will they learn what they should from days like Saturday?

Asked after the game if another kicking-game meltdown (this time a blocked punt recovered by the Sooners for a touchdown) would convince him to change the responsibilities of much-maligned special-teams coordinator Jeff Banks, Sarkisian offered a firm, "No."

He went even farther than that when asked if he'd ever give up play-calling duties. That elicited a, "No chance."

In his defense, this is a program that made the national semifinals in two of the last three years, and was ranked above every other team in the sport on Saturday morning. As Sarkisian pointed out, one ugly loss doesn't mean the whole program is crumbling.

"I think there's a ton of belief in what we're doing," he said.

But when he gets another chance, with everything on the line, will Sarkisian believe in his quarterback? Will he believe in his play caller?

To do that, he'll need to believe that the narratives are wrong.

articles.title: No-call cost Alabama football a chance, but not the Georgia game | Goodbread
articles.summary: An no-call on a clear example of pass interference cost Alabama football a chance to beat Georgia, but UA coach Kalen DeBoer had the right reaction.
articles.body:
It would've been easy for Alabama football coach Kalen DeBoer to blast the officiating in the aftermath of the Crimson Tide's 20-17 loss to Georgia on Saturday, Oct. 10, at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Minutes earlier, he'd just witnessed a brutally bad no-call by an official who had an up-close view of Bulldogs free safety KJ Bolden running directly over Alabama wide receiver Rico Scott in the final minutes on a deep pass into the end zone.

And really, what does DeBoer have to lose?

The penalties for SEC head coaches who publicly criticize officiating aren't much of a deterrent. The consequence comes at the discretion of league commissioner Greg Sankey, who can issue a reprimand or a fine that we all know wouldn't make a $12.5 million coach even blink. Defensive pass interference was clearly the proper call, and had Bolden been flagged, Alabama would have had a first-and-10 on the Bulldogs 19-yard line with 3:26 remaining and trailing by what was eventually the final score.

A chance to win? Sure. A stolen win? No, it wasn't that.

"We can't put the game in that situation, where the officials come into play. We've got to control what we can control," he said.

DeBoer was livid after the play, and rightly so. Coaching staffs across the league submit plays to SEC headquarters each week that they believe were poorly officiated, and you can bet that one will be first among UA's offerings from this game. But when the Crimson Tide gathers for film review by the coaching staff, nobody will be whining about the no-call on Bolden. Because there were too many other reasons that Alabama can point the thumb for a narrow, well-contested loss.

The short list puts the no-call in better perspective.

∎ Start with the sack of Alabama QB Keelon Russell on the very next play – by Bolden himself, no less – which took the Crimson Tide out of field-goal range and forced a punt. A positive play of any kind, even a short gain with a run, would have given UA kicker Conor Talty, who has yet to miss a field goal all season, a chance to tie the game.

∎ Alabama CB Dijon Lee's inexplicable personal foul on the game's final drive gave Georgia the first down it needed to kneel out the clock. Absent that, UA might've been able to get the ball back for one more drive. Alabama safety Keon Sabb was clearly peeved by it. "It wasn't our standard, and it will be addressed," he said.

∎ The UA pass rush was largely non-existent, giving a smart, veteran quarterback in Gunner Stockton far too much time to throw. Time and again, he was able to find receivers on an 18-for-22 passing night with a clean pocket.

∎ Georgia's running game tore through UA's defense for 206 yards on 39 carries, a big reason the Bulldogs were able to overcome miserably bad field position for much of the night.

There were other factors in the loss for Alabama, to be sure, but that summarizes much of what drove the outcome. The Crimson Tide (5-1, 3-1 SEC) might or might not see the Bulldogs again this season. After all, they played a second time last year after meeting in the SEC title game, and a rematch isn't at all out of the question.

What they won't see is a better team than the Bulldogs for the rest of the regular season. There are some big challenges remaining, with a road trip at Tennessee next among them. But the Crimson Tide came up just short against what very well might be the best team in the nation. A bad no-call by an official didn't help.

But it wasn't the reason for the loss, either.

Tuscaloosa News columnist Chase Goodbread is also the weekly co-host of Crimson Cover TV on WVUA-23. Reach him at cgoodbread@gannett.com. Follow on X.com @chasegoodbread.

articles.summary: All you need to know about the road ahead for the Chiefs and how to watch their next game.
articles.body:
The Chiefs couldn't have asked for a better start to the season, with four wins in four games — including two over AFC West opponents.

articles.title: Ducks beat the winless Flames 4-2 in Calgary to start a home-and-home series
articles.summary: CALGARY, Alberta (AP) — Ryan Poehling broke a tie with a short-handed goal at 5:35 of the third period, but was injured on the play in the Anaheim Ducks' 4-2...
articles.body:
CALGARY, Alberta (AP) — Ryan Poehling broke a tie with a short-handed goal at 5:35 of the third period, but was injured on the play in the Anaheim Ducks' 4-2 victory over the winless Calgary Flames on Saturday night to start a home-and-home series.

The teams will meet against Tuesday night in Anaheim.

Poehling was injured when he slid into the post and Flames goalie Dustin Wolf. Poehling, who also had an assist, didn't return to the game.

Jackson Lacombe, Frank Vatrano and Nikita Nesterenko also scored for Anaheim (4-1-0), which won a second road game in two nights after a 5-1 win over the Winnipeg Jets. The Ducks have won their first three road games to start a season for the first time.

Ville Husso stopped 27 shots in his first start of the season.

Morgan Frost and Aydar Suniev scored for Calgary (0-5-0), which started a season with five straight losses for the first time.

Matt Coronato had two assists and Dustin Wolf stopped 24 shots.

articles.title: Kalen DeBoer, Alabama football players respond to Dijon Lee Jr. foul
articles.summary: Kalen DeBoer and Alabama football players gave their thoughts on Dijon Lee's costly personal foul against Georgia. Here's what they said.
articles.body:
Alabama football coach Kalen DeBoer didn't mince words with defensive back Dijon Lee Jr. after a late personal foul with the game on the line against Georgia .

The Crimson Tide was down 20-17 with 2:19 to play when a flag was called on Lee, who got in a shoving match with Bulldogs senior defensive tackle Josh Horton on second down. Lee, a sophomore, was seen getting an earful from DeBoer on the sideline. The ABC broadcast reported that they believed they saw DeBoer tell Lee, "You cost us the game."

Lee was embraced by defensive back Red Morgan as DeBoer to express his displeasure, which Lee appeared receptive to.

"We preach emotional maturity, and I really feel strong across the board we had that with our team, and didn't," DeBoer said on the matter after the game.

"We never expected that to happen," DeBoer continued. "If you're out there giving everything you've got, you've got to give yourself a chance. Emotional maturity is what it comes down to and, you know, we've been pretty good at that the last two years. Obviously, when a moment comes up like we had just now, we didn't respond the right way."

Team captain and defensive back Bray Hubbard said that the team has to "stay locked in" when emotions run high late.

"We talk about having no foolish penalties," Hubbard said. "That's kind of a crucial penalty. It was third down. We hold 'em there, they have to punt the ball and give the ball back to our offense. Instead, chains move and as soon as the ref blows the whistle, time starts ticking. ... We basically gave them that."

Fellow defensive back Keon Sabb called Lee his "brother 'til I die." He said he tries to "uplift" Lee, but he is firm that there is a "standard" at Alabama .

"He wasn't up to that standard, and it will be addressed," Sabb said.

Emilee Smarr covers Alabama basketball and Crimson Tide athletics for The Tuscaloosa News. She can be reached via email at esmarr@usatodayco.com.

articles.title: Singapore boasts F1 night race, but visitors face a remarkable problem
articles.summary: The Singapore Grand Prix is known as one of the most spectacular night races on the Formula 1 calendar. However, the late timing presents a significant disad...
articles.body:
The Singapore Grand Prix is known as one of the most spectacular night races on the Formula 1 calendar. However, the late timing presents a significant disadvantage for visitors and journalists: public transport stops shortly after midnight. Anyone who wants to watch the entire race and also enjoy the concerts afterwards risks missing the last metro.

The Singapore Grand Prix starts at 8:00 p.m . local time on Sunday and, according to the official schedule, runs until approximately 10:00 p.m. This makes it one of the few races held entirely in the dark. The spectacle does not end when the drivers cross the finish line, either. The organisers offer visitors an extensive entertainment programme featuring performances by international artists.

However, visitors who depend on public transport need to keep a close eye on the time. Although the metro schedule has been extended specifically for the Formula 1 weekend, the extension is limited. The last trains depart at around 12:30 a.m. on Friday and Saturday, half an hour later than usual. On Sunday, some services run slightly longer, but even then public transport stops relatively early. Most metro services stop running at around 12:45 a.m.

Public transport stops shortly after midnight

Singapore has an extensive metro network, which plays an important role in transporting the hundreds of thousands of visitors during race weekend. Because of the numerous road closures around the Marina Bay Street Circuit , the organisers strongly advise visitors to use public transport.

Singapore's Land Transport Authority, LTA, has therefore adjusted the timetable. On Friday and Saturday, the last trains departed from centrally located City Hall at 12:30 a.m. On Sunday, this was extended by 15 minutes to 12:45 a.m.

However, not everyone departs from City Hall. Depending on the exit visitors use, the stations Promenade, Nicoll Highway, Esplanade, Bayfront and Raffles Place are also important departure points. According to the timetable, the last train from Promenade towards Expo departs at around 12:46 a.m.

That does not mean travellers can reach every station until that time. The final departure times vary by line and direction. Those who need to change trains may also find that a connecting service has already stopped running. The metro connection to Changi Airport does not benefit from the extended timetable either. The organisers also warn visitors to expect crowds when leaving the circuit. As a result, it may take some time before they actually reach a metro station.

To make matters worse, the organisers have scheduled some of the biggest performances for after the Formula 1 sessions. The Killers, among others, were on the programme on Saturday evening. According to the schedule, the American rock band's concert did not end until 11:45 p.m.

On Sunday evening, Lana Del Rey is the headline act closing the programme at the Padang Stage. Her performance begins at 10:25 p.m. and runs until 11:55 p.m. Anyone attending the full concert then has only around 45 minutes before the last metros depart from the main stations. During that time, visitors must leave the concert grounds, make their way through the crowds and reach the correct station.

The situation becomes even more difficult if the race is delayed. A serious crash or a rain shower resulting in a red flag could cause the Grand Prix to finish much later than the scheduled 10:00 p.m. Singapore is also known as a circuit where the safety car is regularly required.

Saturday already showed that this is far from an unlikely scenario. The sprint race started half an hour late because of heavy rain, which also delayed qualifying by 30 minutes. If a similar delay occurs during the Grand Prix, visitors will have considerably less time to use public transport afterwards.

Alternative transport also creates problems

Anyone who misses the last metro is largely dependent on a taxi or a ride through services such as Grab and Gojek. During race weekend, however, this is not as straightforward as usual either. Because of the road closures around the Marina Bay Street Circuit, drivers may pick up passengers only at designated locations. Visitors must therefore first walk to one of the official pick-up points outside the circuit. Depending on the exit, this can mean a substantial walk.

A taxi ride also comes with an additional cost. For journeys from certain official taxi stands, a surcharge applies on all three race days between 9:30 p.m. and midnight, on top of the regular taxi fare and any other applicable charges. Rates for various services may also rise when many visitors request transport at the same time. Potential waiting times are another uncertain factor. Some temporary pick-up points remain available until 1:00 a.m., but that does not guarantee that a driver will be immediately available at that time.

Singapore GP: a spectacular night race that ends at midnight

The limited timetable also creates problems for journalists. After the finish and podium ceremony, interviews with drivers and media sessions with team principals are still scheduled. There is a considerable chance that the final sessions will take place well after midnight, when most metro services have already stopped running. As a result, not only journalists who are still working after the event but also visitors who want to remain at the circuit longer will quickly find themselves dependent on alternative transport.

The Singapore Grand Prix presents itself as the 'Home of the F1 Night Race', as can be seen in large lettering on and around the circuit and public transport stations. With its spectacular illuminated street circuit and extensive entertainment programme, the organisers certainly live up to that name. Precisely for that reason, it is striking that public transport is so poorly aligned with the event's nocturnal character. Visitors who want to enjoy the race and everything surrounding it to the fullest must therefore allow for a relatively early departure or arrange alternative transport.

articles.title: Bayern Munich star Lennart Karl most valuable U-18 player in the world
articles.summary: The FC Bayern star has made a great impression in his young career.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich have another reason to be excited about the future, with Lennart Karl ranked as the most valuable under-18 player in world football according to Transfermarkt (via @iMiaSanMia ).

The FC Bayern attacking talent tops the list with an estimated market value of €60 million, putting him ahead of Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman and Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha, who are both valued at €50 million. Karl is listed at 18 years old, underlining just how quickly his stock has risen.

For Bayern, this is another encouraging sign that their investment in young talent is paying off. Karl has already generated plenty of excitement with his performances, and his emergence gives the club another exciting attacking option for both the present and the future. With Vincent Kompany willing to trust young players, Karl has a genuine opportunity to turn his potential into a permanent place in the first team.

The competition is hardly short of talent, either. Paris Saint-Germain's Ibrahim Mbaye and Arsenal's Max Dowman are among the highly rated youngsters on the list, while Borussia Dortmund prospect Konstantinos Karetsas sits sixth with a €35 million valuation.

Still, Karl occupies the top spot, which is no small achievement in a generation packed with promising young footballers.

Of course, market value is not the same as proven quality, and Bayern supporters will want to see Karl continue developing rather than get carried away by a Transfermarkt figure. However, the €60 million valuation reflects the enormous potential people see in him.

The big question now is how far Karl can go. If he continues on his current trajectory, Bayern Munich could have another homegrown star on their hands. The hype is growing, the valuation is climbing, and FC Bayern fans have every reason to be excited about what comes next.

articles.title: The Single Most Important Stat From Georgia/Alabama
articles.summary: Georgia played solid second half defense and Gunner Stockton completed 82% of his passes. But if you’re looking for a stat that explains how Georgia pulled a...
articles.body:
Georgia played solid second half defense and Gunner Stockton completed 82% of his passes. But if you're looking for a stat that explains how Georgia pulled an (admittedly mild) upset in Tuscaloosa on Saturday night, here it is:

Alabama came into the game giving up an average of 78.6 yards per game on the ground. Against Georgia they surrendered 206.

If I'd told you coming into this one that the Athenians would play without both Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens and still rush for over 200 yards against the nation's #9 ranked rushing defense you would have had me sent for evaluation and asked if I heard that from a giant invisible rabbit named Harvey. The improbably solid effort put up by Dwight Phillips, Bo Walker and Nick Peal was a team effort that we can't celebrate enough.

I'm not thrilled about the prospect of rolling with that trio for the rest of the season and hope Bowens and Frazier return sooner rather than later. But if the Bulldog offensive line continues to open up holes like the ones they flayed open in the Bama defense on Saturday, I expect we'll still be okay. Until later…

articles.title: Moto2 race red-flagged after big Turn 1 crash involving multiple riders
articles.summary: The Moto2 race in Indonesia began with a big crash that involved four riders. The session had to be red-flagged as well.
articles.body:
The Moto2 race in Indonesia began with a big crash that involved four riders. The session had to be red-flagged as well.

Heading into Turn 1 after the start, future MotoGP rider Daniel Holgado lost control of his bike and hit his teammate David Alonso. Holgado also took out American Racing rider Joe Roberts, while the fuel tank that came off Alonso's bike hit Collin Veijer's KTM. Luckily, all four riders were back on their feet after the incident.

As the race was red-flagged before three laps were completed, the riders will now line up on the original grid.

Alonso's bike cannot be repaired in such a short amount of time, however, Holgado and Veijer's team are working hard to have the only bike they have ready for the restart. Watch the incident below!

Moto2 race in Indonesia begins with Turn 1 crash

articles.title: Colts rule out 5 players for Week 5 vs. Steelers, including key defenders
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have ruled out five players for Sunday's Week 5 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' Week 5 opponent, the Indianapolis Colts , have ruled out several players for Sunday's matchup.

Courtesy of the final Week 5 injury report, the Colts ruled out five players for their game against the Steelers : linebacker Jaylon Carlies, wide receiver Ashton Dulin, defensive end Arden Key, tight end Will Mallory, and wide receiver Darius Slayton.

After missing the first 11 games of the 2025 season, Carlies has had a concerning injury history. He's appeared in the first four games for Indianapolis but suffered a rib injury in the Colts' Week 4 win that ultimately led to him getting ruled out in Week 5.

Dulin previously suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 and missed the team's next two games. Despite returning in Week 4, Dulin suffered a hamstring injury, which ultimately led to him being sidelined for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

Key has appeared in every game so far for Indianapolis this season but suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 4 win over the Washington Commanders . He was unable to log a single practice this week and was ruled out on Friday.

Mallory, listed as the fourth-string tight end on the Colts' depth chart, put together a strong performance in the team's preseason opener before suffering a thumb sprain at training camp practice on August 20. He was placed on injured reserve on August 31 and returned to Week 5 practice on Wednesday as a full participant, but the Colts decided to hold him out for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

Slayton, who spent his first seven years with the New York Giants and has yet to make his debut with the Colts, was originally designated as questionable with a knee injury for Week 5 before the team downgraded him to out on Saturday.

For up-to-date Steelers coverage, including any roster news and injury updates, follow us on X @TheSteelersWire and give our Facebook page a like.

articles.title: Joe Mazzulla on what Jayson Tatum showed us in Celtics' preseason Sixers blowout
articles.summary: The St. Louis native went a long way toward allaying lingering health concerns from how last season ended.
articles.body:
Even though he returned to play from his Achilles tendon injury at the end of last season, there have been concerns about the health of star Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum given he ended that campaign on the bench, unable to play in Boston's final playoff game of 2026 postseason.

But St. Louis native helped allay some of those concerns in the Celtics' 144-106 demolition of the Philadelphia 76ers at TD Garden Saturday (Oct. 10) night. Tatum put up an efficient 23 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists. Boston head coach Joe Mazzulla spoke to how that outing sets the stage to put those concerns behind Tatum, saying that "tonight ... I thought he had good carryover from what we're asking him to do on both ends of the floor."

"His defensive activity was good," he added. "I thought offensively he had great flow, the ball found him, but he was able to create opportunities for him and his teammates."

"And so I thought to carry over from what our expectation is for him on both sides of the ball is one step of doing it there and continue to get better and better from it," said the Celtics coach. "But I thought his cardio looked good. His decision making looked good. His activity was good."

And when he was on the floor during the competitive portion of the exhibition tilt, so did Tatum's play – not that we need to tell you as much.
